title: Automix song analysis
description: One song's analysis as the planner reads it (src/automix/automix.js results; made by the analysis worker in src/vendor/automix, BitChord's analyzer). Times are seconds of the song's own timeline. Both apps produce and read this shape.

analysisVersion.description: Which producer and build made it: each app writes its own (extension 'bc8.v1', phone 'ayham.2'). An analysis with another app's or another build's value is redone, never mixed.

musicVideo.description: Analysed from a music video's audio. Loop mixes are refused for it: its bars rarely match the song's.

bassCurve.description: Kick and bass level (Orchard bass_curve): 35-140 Hz RMS every 0.25 s from 0 s, 1 = the song's usual level (75th percentile of per-second means). Beatless passages read near 0; Automix v2's bridge and muffle read it. null: not measured.

subBassRatio.description: Production style (Orchard's): log10 of the energy at 25-60 Hz over 60-250 Hz, whole song. Automix v2 never overlaps two songs 0.9 or more apart. null: not measured.

chroma.description: The whole song's pitch-class profile, C to B, summed to 1 (Orchard earmark chroma). Automix v2's key score uses its cosine. null: not measured.

chromaCurve.description: Pitch classes every 0.5 s (16384-point spectra, peaks 65 Hz-2.1 kHz): each frame summed to 1, its weight against the song's median frame (drum-only frames weigh little). Automix v2's bridge checks the keys where two songs meet from it. null: not measured.

loudnessCurve.description: K-weighted (ITU BS.1770) mean square every 0.1 s, in dB (floor -120). Automix v2 reads a region's EBU R128 gated loudness from it. null: not measured.

contentEndSec.description: Where the music ends (trailing silence cut). Advanced AutoDJ (version 2) plans its mix-out against this. null: not measurable.

bpm.description: Tempo of the whole song's beat grid.

firstDownbeatSec.description: Anchor of the constant bar grid: downbeats at firstDownbeatSec + k * 4 * beatIntervalSec.

gridConfidence.description: How well the constant grid fits. Blends need >= the planner's MIN_GRID_CONFIDENCE; long blends are shortened on a weak grid.

tailGrid.description: The grid fitted to the song's last part only, used for the outgoing side (asOutgoing). null: the end has no usable grid. Absent: older analysis, the whole-song grid is used.

headBeats.description: Beat This! model beats in the song's opening (the incoming loop is searched here).

tailBeats.description: Beat This! model beats in the song's ending (the outgoing loop is searched here).

energyCurve.description: Loudness energy in consecutive 16-beat windows from 0 s (Auto blend length reads 'calm' as under 0.7 of the mean).

introEndSec.description: Where full energy starts. A blend lands the incoming song's pre-full-energy phrase at its end.

loudness20Hz.description: Optional. RMS of the decoded audio in consecutive 50 ms windows from 0 s (channel 0, every 16th sample: what the loop planner reads), for the overview's waveform and loop checks. The pair fixtures carry it beside the analysis.

ytLoudnessDb.description: Optional. YouTube's loudness for this video: playerConfig.audioConfig.loudnessDb of the player response = trackAbsoluteLoudnessLkfs - loudnessTargetLkfs (target -7 LKFS). YouTube web only turns loud songs down, never quiet ones up: element volume = player volume x min(1, 10^(-loudnessDb/20)) (measured 2026-11-17 in Firefox: +1.76 dB -> x0.8166, +0.85 dB -> x0.9068, -1.26 dB -> x1). A deck replacing YouTube's sound plays at that same level. Both decks level against this. Extension: read in the page from the player response (#movie_player getPlayerResponse(), or the /youtubei/v1/player answer). Phone: the same field of its InnerTube player request (BitChord: StreamResolver.loudnessDbFor). null: YouTube gave none.

ytPerceptualLoudnessDb.description: Optional. playerConfig.audioConfig.perceptualLoudnessDb when YouTube sends it: the track's absolute loudness in LKFS (equal to trackAbsoluteLoudnessLkfs; loudnessDb is this minus loudnessTargetLkfs, -7). Prefer: ytLoudnessDb to match what YouTube's own player does (a deck replacing the player must sound like it); ytPerceptualLoudnessDb, when present, to compare two songs' absolute loudness, else ytLoudnessDb - 7 (Metrolist's conversion).

vocals.description: open-unmix vocal mask in windows: curve[i] is how sung the moment startSec + i / fps is (0..1; > 0.25 counts as sung). Used where a song has no synced lyrics.

downbeats.description: Bar lines. A loop runs from one downbeat to the one N bars later (within a quarter beat), so its seam is the music's own bar line.
